CARGO AHOY / PRIVACY POLICY

Privacy policy

Last updated: November 9, 2026

Dunkstone (“we”) makes Cargo Ahoy. This policy explains what happens to your information when you play.

What the game keeps on your device

Your progress, gold, collection, settings and privacy answers are saved on your device. We don’t ask for your name, email address or an account. Settings shows a support code: a random ID made on your device. It’s attached to the game’s analytics and crash reports (below), and you can quote it when you contact us.

Ads

Cargo Ahoy shows ads, and Unity LevelPlay chooses which partner shows each one. To show and measure ads, LevelPlay and its partners may collect:

  • your device’s advertising identifier, if you allow it (on iPhone, through Apple’s tracking alert; on Android, unless you’ve deleted it in your phone’s settings)
  • your IP address, and the rough location it implies
  • your device type, operating system and language
  • which ads you saw and tapped

Each partner handles this data under its own privacy policy:

  • Unity LevelPlay and Unity Ads
  • Google AdMob
  • Meta Audience Network
  • Liftoff
  • Mintegral
  • DT Exchange
  • InMobi

Analytics and crash reports

We use Google’s Firebase to learn how the game is played and to fix crashes:

  • Google Analytics for Firebase records gameplay events, such as runs started and finished, heights reached, ads watched and purchases made, along with your support code, Firebase’s app instance ID, your device type, operating system and the rough location your IP address implies.
  • Firebase Crashlytics sends a report when the game crashes: the device, the operating system, the state of the app and your support code. It never includes your saved game.
  • Firebase Remote Config downloads the game’s settings, such as ad timing, so we can adjust them without an update.

Nothing is sent before you’ve answered the consent questions. If you don’t consent, analytics runs in Google’s consent mode, which sends events without identifiers. Google handles this data under the Firebase privacy and security terms and Google’s privacy policy.

Your choices

  • Consent: where the law requires it, Google’s form asks for your consent before any ad loads.
  • Tracking on iPhone: Apple’s alert asks whether apps may track you. You can change this in iOS Settings at any time.
  • Advertising ID on Android: you can reset or delete it in your phone’s Settings › Privacy › Ads. Ads then stop being personalised by it.
  • Changing your mind: where the law gives you these choices, the game’s Settings shows Privacy choices or Your Privacy Choices.
  • Removing ads: Remove Ads stops interstitial ads. Ads you choose to watch stay available.

Purchases

Apple or Google handles any purchase. We never see your payment details. Unity IAP handles the store for us. To complete and restore purchases it records your purchase history and an ID for your device, under Unity’s privacy policy.

Leaderboards, reminders, ratings and sharing

If you’re signed in to Game Center on iPhone, or Google Play Games on Android, your best heights are posted to its leaderboards, under Apple’s or Google’s privacy policy. Reminders are local notifications planned on your device; the game asks before sending any (Android 13 and later ask for permission too), and we don’t run a notification server. The rating prompt and the share sheet are your phone’s own, from Apple or Google; we receive nothing from them.

Children

Cargo Ahoy is not directed at children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect their information. If you believe a child has given us information, contact us.

Your rights

Depending on where you live, you may have the right to access, correct or delete your personal information, to object to its use, and to complain to your privacy regulator. To use these rights, contact us with the support code from the game’s Settings: it’s what links your analytics and crash reports to you, and we can delete them with it. We don’t hold your name or email address, so requests about ad data may go to the partners above.

Transfers and retention

Google, Unity and the ad partners may process data outside your country, including in the United States. They keep it for the periods their policies state; Crashlytics keeps crash reports for 90 days. Saved game data stays on your device until you delete the game.

Contact

Privacy contact: contact@dunkstone.com.

Changes

We’ll post any change here and update the date above.
